changes.change: Two fixes: (a) Extracted _seed_facts_once() + _ensure_seeded() lazy-init guard. The startup event is unreliable in TestClient, so /api/facts now calls _ensure_seeded() to guarantee the seed runs on first read. (b) POST /api/facts now uses FactCreate (the 3-field input model) instead of Fact (the 7-field full model) so the client does not have to send server-assigned fields.

Removed reset_registry() + the 3-fact re-seed from Orchestrator.__init__. Previously the orchestrator was constructed on every /api/orchestrator/process HTTP request, so every request was wiping the in-memory facts and re-seeding with a different Technical statement. The orchestrator now leaves the facts registry alone; seeding belongs to the app startup only.

Added 2 regression tests: (1) test_orchestrator_does_not_wipe_operator_facts -- POSTs a unique-marked fact, calls /api/orchestrator/process, asserts the fact is still there. Verified the test catches the old bug by manual replay. (2) test_evaluation_suite_is_deterministic -- runs /api/eval/run 3 times, strips runId+timestamp (the only non-deterministic fields), asserts the rest is byte-identical. Closes OPEN_ITEMS B2.

payload.description: The Tauri shell, third_party_assistant.py REPL, discovery_agent, monitor_agent, and InventoryAgent were never run end-to-end against each other. D5 wires them into a single user-facing flow using Ollama tool calling -- the operator types a natural-language question and a local LLM (aegis 1.5B Qwen2) loops over tool calls to the FastAPI audit server until it has an answer.
design_notes: The Ollama Python package was NOT added to requirements.txt. The REPL uses urllib.request, which is stdlib and already used elsewhere in the project.
The 9 tool functions are all wrappers around FastAPI endpoints. The REPL does NOT import from src/engines or src/agents directly -- same boundary rule tests/ follows.
A small Ollama schema builder (_ollama_schema) parses each function docstring for Google-style Args: sections. Avoids the ollama Python package and pydantic.
The live end-to-end test is skip-guarded with executable documentation (the skip message names the exact host feature missing).
third_party_assistant.py chat command spawns the REPL as a subprocess rather than importing it. This keeps the REPL out of the runtime import graph entirely.

grade.post_state: All 7 real issues closed. The script is now USB-deployable: the install path is derived from the script own location; the script refuses to run on Python < 3.12; pip failures mark the deploy DEGRADED (not COMPLETE); launchers are templated from $InstallPath; the closing step re-derives the Merkle chain and prints MATCH/BROKEN.
grade.pre_state: 10 issues found; 7 of them real. Top: hardcoded C:\OrderGetItRight install path, no Python version check, no verify_chain after deploy, launchers hardcoded install path, no project-root marker check.

1_no_ambient_state.change: Step 0a now refuses to run unless pyproject.toml AND 02_Technical\ exist in the cwd. A silent misfire (running from Downloads and copying the wrong files) is worse than a refusal.

2_install_path_resolution.change: Default install path is now derived from $PSScriptRoot (sibling of deploy/). USB-deployable: a script at E:\OrderGetItRight\deploy\deploy.ps1 defaults to E:\OrderGetItRight. The hardcoded C:\OrderGetItRight is gone. -InstallPath still overrides.

3_python_version_gate.change: Step 2 checks the Python version. Refuses to proceed with < 3.12 (the build uses PEP 695 syntax; 3.11 will load the source and crash on import). Throws, not warns.

4_pip_is_best_effort.change: Step 3 catches pip install failure. A failed package sets $DeployDegraded=$true; the closing banner says DEGRADED, not COMPLETE. A deploy that reports COMPLETE must be a deploy that actually completed.

5_tauri_default_off.change: Step 5 only invokes build-tauri.ps1 if $env:OGIR_BUILD_TAURI=1 AND -SkipTauri was not passed. Default: skipped (Tauri takes 2-5 minutes and is not part of the runtime path).

6_templated_launchers.change: Step 4 templates every .bat from $InstallPath and $PythonExe at write time. The previous hardcoded C:\OrderGetItRight in launcher bodies is gone. USB-relative launchers work on the host that ran the deploy.

7_verify_chain_final.change: Step 6 runs src.verify_chain in the real (non-dry-run) flow and inspects stdout for "RESULT: MATCH". On mismatch, the deploy is marked DEGRADED and the script exits 2 (not 0). A deploy that did not verify the chain is a deploy that did not deploy.

8_yes_flag.change: -Yes skips the confirmation prompt. Default: prompt before mutating. The -Yes flag is the unattended mode (operator double-clicks and walks away). The prompt is a second-line defence against typo install paths.

payload.note: A3 closed. The seed-on-POST gap was the residual foot-gun: the test that was supposed to close A3 (test_seed_facts_preserves_operator_facts_across_reseed) was failing because POST /api/facts did not call _ensure_seeded(). Modern FastAPI TestClient does not fire the lifespan handler before the first request, so the seed facts were missing on a fresh process. The first operator POST in a fresh process would land in a registry with no seed facts. Fix: POST /api/facts now calls _ensure_seeded() before adding the operator fact. _seed_facts_once() is guarded by , so this is safe -- it never wipes operator facts. Test also reinforced: forces a clean baseline, asserts seed categories are present before the operator add, asserts operator id is not a seed id, asserts re-seed does not duplicate, asserts second re-seed is idempotent. test_smoke.py 28/28 pass; full suite 76 pass + 1 skip (D5 E2E).

payload.statement: Order Get It Right enforces the four-gate audit model (Deception / BBFB / Valuation / Decision).
All deception detections use the deterministic 3.10 (54 patterns, R1-R4 applied) ontology.
BBFB engine uses LAW / GRACE / FRUIT decomposition with quadratic penalty and weighted FRUIT score.

audit_gated_v3_10.DD-006_context: Three 'could' usages, all in capability/description contexts (e.g. 'Congress determined in 1871 that state institutions could not be trusted to vindicate federal rights'). One 'maybe' in a hedge context ('Maybe one can offer a different flavor of this argument...').
audit_gated_v3_10.DD-041_context: DD-041 is the R3-gated pattern (Hedging Loop, renamed from Multilingual Hedging Loop). The gate requires the 'could be' indicator AND a sentence with NO implementation signal. The match here is on 'maybe' (not 'could be'), so the gate was bypassed entirely. R3 only covers 'could be' -- the 'maybe' surface form is unchecked.
audit_gated_v3_10.interpretation: DD-006 is the R2-gated pattern; the gate requires an obligation verb in the same sentence. None of the four 'could' sentences contain must/shall/will/agree/commit/promise/guarantee, so the gate SHOULD have suppressed DD-006 here. The fact that it did not is a real R1-R4 gate gap: the gate's _OBLIGATION_VERBS set does not include 'determined' (which appears in the first sentence as 'Congress determined in 1871 that state institutions could not be trusted') -- this is a structural determination, not an obligation, but the lexical set was the wrong list.

r1_r4_gate_gap_discovered: DD-006 R2 gate does not cover the 'maybe' indicator. R2 only added an obligation-verb check for 'could' / 'to clarify'. 'maybe' is also a DD-006 indicator and is unchecked. The text 'Maybe one can offer a different flavor of this argument' is a meta-argument hedge, not a programmatic ambiguity; R2 needs to be extended.

DD-041 R3 gate only covers 'could be'. The DD-041 indicator set includes 'perhaps', 'maybe', 'potentially', 'it depends', 'possibly' -- none of these are R3-gated. R3 needs to be extended to cover the full DD-041 indicator set, or the 'maybe' indicator should be moved to a different pattern (e.g. DD-013 Logic Drift which is the better home for 'maybe' as a hedge).

DD-006 R2 _OBLIGATION_VERBS set is incomplete. 'determined' (past-tense legislative determination) is a structural obligation marker that should be in the set. 'must', 'shall', 'will' alone are forward-looking; the gate should also cover past-tense structural markers like 'determined', 'established', 'ruled', 'enacted'.
